answer: Identity here is welded to silicon. Each key is minted inside a quartz chip that signs its own boot, and peers verify the factory root before trusting a word it says. Cloning is cheap; buying genuine chips is not, so a fake fleet pays parts for every ghost. A ledger built this way stands like a jetty: each pile driven deep, none doing the work of two. And every summit marker must be walked to, attested at the rock itself, not drawn from below.
